#+TITLE: Vendor Directory: Managing Submodules
#+AUTHOR: Claude
#+DATE: [2024-10-01 Tue]

* Introduction
This directory (=/vendor=) contains third-party dependencies managed as Git submodules. This README explains how to work with these submodules effectively, with a focus on the Threlte submodule.

* Adding a New Submodule
We use a custom script to add new submodules. Here's the script for adding the Threlte submodule:

#+BEGIN_SRC bash
#!/bin/bash
SUBMODULE_PATH="packages/vendor/threlte"
REPO_URL="git@github.com:threlte/threlte.git"
git submodule add $REPO_URL $SUBMODULE_PATH
#+END_SRC

This script:
1. Defines the submodule path and repository URL.
2. Adds the submodule to our repository.

* Configuring Sparse Checkout
After adding the submodule, you can configure sparse checkout to only retrieve specific files. However, this step is currently commented out in the script:

#+BEGIN_SRC bash
git config core.sparseCheckout true
# Create the sparse-checkout file
cat <<EOT > .git/modules/packages/vendor/threlte/info/sparse-checkout
packages/*/src/**/*.js
packages/*/src/**/*.ts
packages/*/src/**/*.svelte
EOT
#+END_SRC

If you decide to use sparse checkout:
1. Uncomment these lines in the script.
2. This will enable sparse checkout for the submodule.
3. It will create a sparse-checkout file specifying which files to include.

* Fetching Submodule Content
The script for fetching submodule content is also commented out:

#+BEGIN_SRC bash
cd $SUBMODULE_PATH
# Fetch the content
git fetch --depth 1 origin main
git checkout main
# Go back to the root directory
cd ../../..
#+END_SRC

If you decide to use this:
1. Uncomment these lines in the script.
2. It will navigate to the submodule directory.
3. Fetch the latest changes from the main branch with a depth of 1.
4. Checkout the main branch.
5. Return to the root directory.

* Updating Submodules
We use a separate script to update submodules:

#+BEGIN_SRC bash
#!/bin/bash
SUBMODULE_PATH="packages/vendor/threlte"
# Navigate to the submodule directory
cd $SUBMODULE_PATH
# Fetch the latest changes
git fetch origin main
# Reset to the latest commit on main
git reset --hard origin/main
# Update the working tree
git read-tree -mu HEAD
# Go back to the root of the main repository
cd ../../..
# Stage the submodule update
git add $SUBMODULE_PATH
echo "Threlte submodule updated. Don't forget to commit the changes in the main repository."
#+END_SRC

This script:
1. Navigates to the submodule directory.
2. Fetches the latest changes from the main branch.
3. Resets the submodule to the latest commit on main.
4. Updates the working tree.
5. Returns to the root directory and stages the submodule update.
6. Reminds you to commit the changes in the main repository.

* Best Practices
1. Always commit and push changes in a submodule directory separately.
2. After updating a submodule, commit the changes in the main repository.
3. Communicate submodule changes to your team to ensure everyone is working with the correct versions.
4. If you decide to use sparse checkout, make sure to uncomment and configure the relevant parts of the script.

* Cloning the Repository with Submodules
When cloning the repository, use one of these methods to include submodules:

** Method 1 (two steps)
#+BEGIN_SRC bash
git clone <repository-url>
cd <repository-name>
git submodule init
git submodule update
#+END_SRC

** Method 2 (one step)
#+BEGIN_SRC bash
git clone --recurse-submodules <repository-url>
#+END_SRC

* Checking Submodule Status
To check the status of all submodules:
#+BEGIN_SRC bash
git submodule status
#+END_SRC

* Running Commands on All Submodules
To run a command on all submodules:
#+BEGIN_SRC bash
git submodule foreach '<command>'
#+END_SRC

By following these guidelines, you can effectively manage third-party dependencies as submodules within your monorepo structure. Note that some features like sparse checkout are currently commented out in the scripts - adjust as needed for your specific use case.
